accepted.statement: The body-parser 2.3.0 package can be triggered to cause a denial‑of‑service by sending a request with trailing bytes after a compressed body. It is pulled in transitively through express and other SDKs, so the vulnerable code can be executed in the application. With a CVSS of 7.5 (score 31.4) and an EPSS of 0.00388, the issue is high‑severity and reachable; upgrade to body-parser 2.4.0, which is clean on the registry.

The npm package cors@2.8.6 is flagged as a possible typosquat of the popular colors package. Although it is used transitively, the name similarity alone does not prove malicious intent, but the suspicion warrants review. Remove the package or replace it with the intended dependency after verification.

The @hono/node-server 2.1.5 module can crash the process when an ECONNRESET occurs during an asynchronous WebSocket upgrade. It is included transitively via the @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, making the crash reachable in the app. The vulnerability has a CVSS of 5.3 (score 26.0) and EPSS 0.00453; upgrade to @hono/node-server 2.1.6 to resolve the issue.

hono 4.13.13 allows mount() and app.mount() to forward a path that bypasses middleware scoped inside the mount prefix, potentially skipping security checks. The package is pulled in transitively via the SDK and also via @hono/node-server, so the bypass can affect the application. It carries a CVSS of 5.3 (score 25.3) and EPSS 0.004; upgrade to hono 4.13.16 to mitigate the risk.

hono 4.13.13 has a flaw where validator('form') skips validation for multipart/form-data requests that contain extra parameters. This code is reachable through the SDK and @hono/node-server, allowing malformed requests to bypass form validation. With a CVSS of 5.3 (score 25.2) and EPSS 0.00392, the issue is moderate; upgrade to hono 4.13.16 to fix the problem.

The @hono/node-server 2.1.5 module parses a backslash in the request path as a path separator, allowing an attacker to bypass path‑based access control at a reverse proxy. This code is reachable transitively via the SDK, so the bypass can be exploited in the application. It has a CVSS of 5.3 (score 24.9) and EPSS 0.00375; upgrading to @hono/node-server 2.1.6 resolves the vulnerability.

fast-uri 3.1.8 is vulnerable to URI‑scheme spoofing via percent‑encoded scheme decoding. The vulnerable module is pulled in transitively through @modelcontextprotocol/sdk → ajv → fast-uri (see the two paths). With a CVSS 6.1, a score of 24.9 (SSVC Track) and an EPS‑S of 0.0025, this issue is relevant to the application. Upgrade fast-uri to 3.1.9 (co‑upgrade ajv 8.20.0 which requires fast-uri ^3.0.1) to remediate.
accepted.next_step: Upgrade fast-uri to 3.1.9 (co‑upgrade ajv as needed)

accepted.statement: hono 4.13.13 has a routing bug where RegExpRouter may skip wildcard middleware for certain routes and for paths containing an encoded line terminator. The package is included transitively via @modelcontextprotocol/sdk (directly and via @hono/node-server). With CVSS 5.3, a score of 24.8 (SSVC Track) and EPS‑S 0.00367, the flaw can affect request handling in the app. Upgrade to hono 4.13.16, which has been rescanned clean.

The Dockerfile uses the base image node:22-slim referenced by a mutable tag, which can be retagged to a vulnerable version. This unpinned reference appears at line 1 of the Dockerfile, making the build image potentially change without notice. With a score of 22.0 (SSVC Track) the risk is significant for supply‑chain integrity. Pin the base image to a specific @sha256 digest and avoid end‑of‑life tags.
accepted.next_step: Pin the base image to a specific digest (e.g., @sha256) and use a supported tag

accepted.statement: The Dockerfile also references node:22-slim by tag at line 9, which suffers the same mutable‑tag issue. Because the tag can be repointed, the built image may unintentionally include vulnerable code. The finding carries a score of 22.0 (SSVC Track), indicating a notable supply‑chain risk. Pin the base image to a specific @sha256 digest and move off end‑of‑life tags.
accepted.next_step: Pin the base image to a specific digest (e.g., @sha256) and use a supported tag

accepted.statement: hono 4.13.13’s csrf() middleware does not validate requests sent via hyperlink auditing (text/ping), potentially allowing CSRF bypass. The vulnerable code is pulled in transitively through @modelcontextprotocol/sdk (directly and via @hono/node-server). With CVSS 5.3, a score of 21.3 (SSVC Track) and EPS‑S 0.00176, this weakness can be exploited in the application. Upgrade to hono 4.13.16, which resolves the issue.

fast-uri 3.1.8 is vulnerable to host confusion due to unchecked WHATWG host canonicalization. The module is included transitively via @modelcontextprotocol/sdk → ajv → fast-uri (both paths shown). With CVSS 4.8, a score of 21.3 (SSVC Track) and EPS‑S 0.00255, the flaw can affect URL handling in the app. Upgrade fast-uri to 3.1.9 (co‑upgrade ajv as required) to fix the issue.
accepted.next_step: Upgrade fast-uri to 3.1.9 (co‑upgrade ajv as needed)

accepted.statement: The esbuild package (npm/esbuild@0.28.2) executes code during its install script. This code runs on the host when the package is installed, even though the package is not imported by the application (reachability: not_imported). Because install‑time code can modify the environment or introduce malicious behavior, the finding is scored 20.0 and marked with an Ssvc of “Track”. No fixed version is provided, so the recommended next step is to monitor the package and consider replacing or upgrading it.
accepted.next_step: Monitor the package and evaluate upgrading or replacement
